title: How to reduce false positives in OFAC screening | Middesk
summary: Reduce avoidable sanctions alerts through better data, full-record comparisons, tested matching rules, and documented decisions that stay current.
body_markdown:
Direct entity screening does not cover an institution's complete sanctions exposure. Under OFAC's 50 Percent Rule, any entity owned 50 percent or more in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, by one or more blocked persons is considered blocked by operation of law, even if the entity does not appear on any government list.


Compliance teams cannot satisfy this requirement using standard Customer Due Diligence (CDD) data alone. Under federal[CDD rule requirements](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/31/1010.230) , financial institutions identify natural persons owning 25 percent or more of equity. In contrast, OFAC's rule considers aggregate corporate ownership and applies to blocked entities as well as individuals. A compliant program analyzes complete corporate ownership hierarchies, calculating aggregate blocked stakes across holding companies.


[Middesk](https://www.middesk.com/products/verify) streamlines watchlist screening by integrating automated watchlist checks directly into the core business verification workflow. By validating entity identities against official state registries and screening businesses and associated individuals against global sanctions databases, Middesk provides the rich secondary data required to minimize false positives. Detailed screening reports include matching scores, source citations, and exact list entries, giving compliance officers the evidence needed to clear false alarms quickly or escalate true sanctions risk.
